cands.name: softfold
cands.summary: The soft fold passes its numeric checks and fails visually; I do not think tuning can rescue it. I built it as approach id "softfold" (first entry of APPROACHES, GLSL plus JavaScript mirror) with the planes dial (1 to 4, starts at 2) and the blend dial a (0 to 0.45, starts at 0.25), and added two drop-downs for the curve and the blend path. It is exact on every plane to 1e-14, has no jump at n = 2, and the shader matches the mirror. But the Julia set for c = -1 is not a row of bodies with beads: it is one swollen mass with X-shaped ridges, about 1.7 across seen along x, and its z = 0.2 slice is larger than its z = 0 slice. The rabbit and the Mandelbrot solid are heaps of shards and flames, much like the pillow round. Raising a toward 0.45 gives dust, not the folded picture. The measured cause: the blend folds the sphere of directions back over itself (the derivative has a negative determinant at 4 to 7% of directions for 2 planes, about 30% for 3 and 4). My argument, checked only for p = 2 and n = 2, is that any continuous mirror-symmetric rule must fold over, crush the seam, or jump there. I built the crush as an extra option ("pinch"): no fold-over, but four huge fins. Time used: 41 minutes.
cands.formulas:
Parameters, read by the shader as uA = (p, a, curve, mix): p = planes (1..4, default 2); a = blend (0..0.45, typed up to 0.49, default 0.25); curve 0 smoothstep / 1 smootherstep; mix 0 great circle / 1 straight line renormalised / 2 pinch.

M(d), the one-plane direction rule for a unit direction d = (x, y, z): phi = atan2(y, x), m = atanh(clamp(z, -0.999999, 0.999999)); M = (cos(n phi)/cosh(nm), sin(n phi)/cosh(nm), tanh(nm)) with nm clamped to +-20. For n == 2 exactly: M = (x^2 - y^2, 2xy, 2z) / (1 + z^2).

F(v) = aprPow(|v|, n) * D(v/|v|), where aprPow is the lab's capped power exp(min(n log max(r, 1e-30), 42)). F = (0,0,0) if |v| < 1e-20 and n > 0. If |v| = 0, d = (1,0,0).

p = 1: D = M(d).

p >= 2:
1. If z < 0, or z == 0 and y < 0: d <- (x, -y, -z), fl = -1; else fl = 1. At the end multiply the y and z of the result by fl.
2. rho = sqrt(y^2 + z^2). If z == 0 or rho <= 1e-15: D = M(d).
3. Otherwise w = pi/p, u = atan2(z, y)/w, j = min(floor(u), p - 1), t = u - j.
   q = clamp((t - a)/(1 - 2a), 0, 1); s = q^2 (3 - 2q) (curve 0) or q^3 (q(6q - 15) + 10) (curve 1).
   ct = cos(tw), st = sin(tw), cw = cos(w), sw = sin(w).
   A = M(x, rho ct, rho st), computed only if s < 1.
   B' = M(x, rho (ct cw + st sw), rho (st cw - ct sw)); B = (B'.x, B'.y cw - B'.z sw, B'.y sw + B'.z cw), computed only if s > 0.
4. Blend to D:
   s <= 0: D = A. s >= 1: D = B.
   mix 0: c = clamp(A.B, -1, 1), e = B - cA, le = |e|. If c < 0 and le < 1e-3: D = A when s < 0.5, else B. Otherwise om = s atan2(le, c), D = cos(om) A + (sin(om)/max(le, 1e-30)) e.
   mix 1: mm = (1 - s)A + sB; if |mm| < 1e-3: D = A when s < 0.5, else B; otherwise D = mm/|mm|.
   mix 2 (pinch, my addition): tau = S(clamp((min(t, 1 - t) - a)/(0.5 - a), 0, 1)). Take P = A if t < 0.5, else B (only that one is computed). Target T = (1, 0, 0) unless |n| is an odd whole number; then with h = w/2 and g = sign(n): T = (x, g rho cos h, g rho sin h) if t < 0.5, else (x, g rho (cw cos h + sw sin h), g rho (sw cos h - cw sin h)). D = great-circle blend of P toward T by tau, using the mix 0 formula with (A, B, s) = (P, T, tau).
5. Turn D back about the x-axis by j w: cj = (y ct + z st)/rho, sj = (z ct - y st)/rho; D <- (D.x, D.y cj - D.z sj, D.y sj + D.z cj).

sqr(v) = pw(v, 2). mul(a, b) is copied unchanged from Sphere inversions with one plane (aprMmul): length min(|a||b|, cap), z-part (Za + Zb)/(1 + Za Zb) with Z = z/|v|, xy-direction the complex product of the two xy-directions. cmap(c) = c (the constant is not folded).

problems: The target is not met. The Julia set for c = -1 is one swollen mass, not a row of bodies, and has no beads on either great circle. Its z = 0.2 slice (17.7% of the picture) is larger than its z = 0 slice (13.7%).

The rabbit, the off-axis basilica and the Mandelbrot solid have no flat torn sheets, but they are heaps of blobs, shards and flames. Off-plane Mandelbrot slices break into 3 pieces at z = 0.1 and 7 at z = 0.25, plus 68 to 90 specks.

No setting looks good. a = 0 to 0.15 gives the fattest, smoothest blob; 0.25 to 0.35 the same with sharper ridges; 0.42 and 0.48 turn to dust with thin spikes on the seams. Smootherstep and the straight blend look the same as the default. 3 and 4 planes are dustier.

The blend folds the sphere of directions over itself: the derivative has a negative determinant at 4.4 to 7.4% of directions for 2 planes and 29 to 36% for 3 and 4, and s2 goes to 0 on the fold lines. The pillow round did not have this.

The brief expected the picture to tend to the folded one as a nears 0.5. The rule does tend to the nearest-plane rule away from the seams, but the rendered picture at a = 0.42 and 0.48 is dust. I did not render the folded baseline again beside it, and part of the dust may be the ray marcher failing on the steep blend (largest stretch 38 at a = 0.45) rather than the set itself. Not separated.

The claim that no tuning can fix this rests on an argument, not a proof, and only for p = 2, n = 2: the seam is a mirror plane, the seam's great circle meets the region it would have to land in only at the +x direction, so a continuous rule must fold over, crush the seam onto the x-axis, or jump. The numbers agree with it (blends fold over, pinch does not).

The pinch (mix 2) is my own addition outside the brief. It has no fold-over and no jump at n = 2, 3, -2, but every seam plane then follows the real map r^2 + c, so for c = -1 the solid grows four enormous fins. Its target for odd powers is a guess that happened to test continuous at n = 3.

A real tear exists for 3 and 4 planes at powers other than 2 whenever a is below the listed t (p=3: 0.22 at n=3; p=4: 0.42 at n=5). The planes dial allows those combinations and nothing warns about them. Two planes have no tear at any power tested.

I added two controls beyond the two dials requested (curve, blend path). The approach texts (about, crush, smooth, round note) were written before the results and partly overstate the rule; the scorecard was not looked at.
I looked at the 38 standard pictures as six contact sheets with 640 px tiles, not one by one at full size. Fine defects could have been missed. The rabbit's connectivity was not checked by slicing.
Not tested: fractional powers, light theme, phone width, the equation presets other than z^n + c, mul() inside a real equation (only compared against the Sphere inversions shader).
Speed ratios are rough: the same rule measured 1.34 against itself on medians in the same run.
Time: 41 minutes, one over the target.

cands.name: axisbulb
cands.summary: Verdict: lathe rings or taffy, not bodies with beads around both great circles. I built approach "axisbulb" (first entry of out/lab2/axisbulb/10-approaches.js, test page dist/lab2-axisbulb.html) with dials k, wobble A, reach and a pinch B that I added. The rule is continuous and exact on z = 0 and y = 0 as claimed, in JavaScript and in the shader. It still misses the target, for three reasons. (1) For a Julia set with c on the x-axis the turn never feeds back into length or angle from the axis, so the basilica is exactly the lathe's body of revolution for every k, A and reach: rings stay rings (0 of 20000 test points differ from the lathe). (2) With k = 5 or -3 the Mandelbrot solid and the rabbit are masses of flames, the exact slice at z = 0 has no thickness (the slice at z = 1e-9 already has 32% less area), and the renderer's distance estimate breaks down. (3) The best variant, k = 1 with A = 0.2 (now the default of the dials), is clean and connected but is the lathe with warped rings: some rings open into ribbons, a few buds appear on the small body, the rabbit is smooth drapery. The pinch is the only dial that changes the basilica; it gives four-finned star bodies, not beads.
cands.formulas:
v = (x, y, z), r = |v|, rho = |(y, z)|, beta = atan2(rho, x) in [0, pi].
Step 1, the lathe power: w = R * (cos(n*beta), sin(n*beta) * y/rho, sin(n*beta) * z/rho), with R = exp(min(n * ln(max(r, 1e-30)), 42)), (y/rho, z/rho) = (1, 0) when rho = 0, and w = 0 when r < 1e-20 and n > 0. For n = 2 the shader's sqr uses w = (x^2 - y^2 - z^2, 2xy, 2xz), capped at 1.74e18 per component.
Step 2, the turn, applied to w: rho' = |(w.y, w.z)|; if rho' = 0 return w. (c, s) = (w.y, w.z) / rho'; r' = |w|.
 - e = (c + i*s)^|k| by |k| complex multiplications starting from 1 (k whole); conjugate e if k < 0. If k = 1, A = 0 and B = 0 return w unchanged.
 - if A != 0: t = clamp((rho'/r') / sin(reach), 0, 1), or t = 1 when reach = 0; W = t^2 * (3 - 2t); phi = A * W * 4*c*s*(c^2 - s^2) (that is A*W*sin(4*turn)); e = e * (cos phi + i sin phi).
 - if B != 0: g = 1 + B * (2*c*s)^2 * (rho'/r')^2 (that is 1 + B sin^2(2*turn) sin^2(n*beta)); else g = 1.
 - F(v) = g * (w.x, rho' * Re e, rho' * Im e), capped at 1.74e18 per component when B != 0.
mul(a, b) = turn(P) with P = (a.x*b.x - a.y*b.y - a.z*b.z, a.x*b.y + b.x*a.y, a.x*b.z + b.x*a.z) capped: copied from the lathe approach, which applies its spin the same way. sqr(v) = turn(lathe square). cmap(c) = c.
Dials (uniform uA in this order): k whole -7..9 default 1; wob = A slider 0..1, typed -1..1, default 0.2; reach degrees 0..90 default 45; pinch = B 0..4 default 0.
In angles, for odd k: (beta, gamma) -> (n*beta, k*gamma + A*W*sin(4*gamma)), length r^n * (1 + B sin^2(2*gamma) sin^2(n*beta)).
Two deliberate departures from the assignment's wording: the turn is applied to the result of the lathe power (identical to the assignment's formula for odd k; for even k it differs by half a turn where sin(n*beta) < 0, and even k is not exact either way), and W is taken at the result's angle from the x-axis, not the input's. Both make pw(v, 2) = sqr(v) = mul(v, v).
e^(i*turn) is raised to k by multiplication and sin(4*turn) is a polynomial, so z = 0 gives z exactly 0 and y = 0 gives y exactly 0.
checks: 1. Exactness (JavaScript mirror, 500 points per plane incl. on and beside the axes and down to 1e-5 from the origin). Worst relative error for n = 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, -1, -2, -3: 1.8e-15, 4.6e-15, 3.6e-15, 5.4e-15, 7.3e-15, 9.1e-16, 1.6e-15, 4.6e-15. Identical on z = 0 and on y = 0, for k = 5, -3, 9, -7 and for k = 1 with wobble 0.2, 0.6 and with pinch 1.5. Limit 1e-6: passed.

1b. Claims: exact on both planes exactly when k = 1 mod 4 (confirmed for 1, 5, 9, -3, -7). k = 3 and -1: z = 0 exact, y = 0 carries the mirror image conj(w)^n. k = 2: neither plane (error 2.0 and 1.4). Planes at 45 degrees: mirror image conj(w)^n for k = 5 and -3 (worst 7.3e-15); the power itself for k = 9, -7 and 1; neither once the pinch is on (by design).
1c. Wobble keeps z = 0 and y = 0 exact for any A: confirmed, including A = 1 with reach 0 and k = -7.

1d. The milder family gamma -> gamma + (k-1)*gamma*W(beta) with W rising smoothly was NOT built: it cannot be continuous. At turn 180 degrees it gives 180*(1 + (k-1)W), so the half y < 0 of the plane z = 0 loses exactness unless (k-1)W is an even whole number, and the rule tears there unless (k-1)W is whole.

2. Continuity, 200000 random pairs 1e-5 apart plus 56000 special pairs (8 half-planes at multiples of 45 degrees, 8 seams half way, both ends of the x-axis, the crushed cones). Largest ratio / 99.9th percentile of the random pairs. n = 2: k=5 10.00 / 9.86; k=-3 6.00 / 5.92; k=1 A=0.2 3.35 / 3.21; k=1 A=0.6 6.31 / 5.95; k=5 A=0.2 10.92 / 10.63; k=1 pinch 1.5 5.58 / 5.48; k=9 18.00 / 17.75; k=-7 A=1 B=4 82.59 / 79.75; lathe 2.00 / 2.00. For comparison Sphere inversions folded on 2 planes: 6073288 (jump).

3. GLSL against JavaScript, 11 settings x 8 powers x 640 points (5120 values each): worst |glsl - js| / (1 + |js|) between 9.2e-5 and 1.6e-4, always at n = 8; 0 values above 2e-3. sqr() against the JavaScript square at most 2.4e-5; mul(a, b) against the lathe product followed by the turn at most 2.5e-5. A point with z = 0 comes back with z exactly 0 in every setting; a point with y = 0 with y exactly 0 (except k = 2, which does not keep that plane). Finite at the origin, on the axes and at 1e18. No shader compile errors, no console errors in any run.

4. Distortion at n = 2, 20000 directions, s1/s2 median / 95th / 99.9th percentile: k=5 2.83 / 4.9 / 174; k=-3 1.99 / 6.4 / 290; k=1 A=0.2 2.84 / 19.5 / 871; k=1 A=0.6 2.32 / 38.6 / 1402; k=5 A=0.2 2.79 / 5.3 / 174; pinch 1.5 1.73 / 19.4 / 871; lathe 2.01 / 19.2 / 871; Sphere inversions one plane 1.00 / 1.0 / 1. The flames of the k = 5 and k = -3 Mandelbrot solid remain with the estimate off and 700 steps, so they are the solid, not only an artefact.

cands.name: pillow2
cands.summary:
ANSWER: yes, the pillow is a rock by nature; the three layouts were not the cause. I built both variants as the first two approaches of a private page (dist/lab2-pillow2.html), made all 48 pictures plus 24 comparison pictures of the one-plane and folded rules, and measured the solids in double precision.

1. With the creases gone the basilica is still ONE LUMP. The angle-true pillow (pillowsmooth: no triangles, no creases, no seams) draws c = -1 as one smooth egg with a single spike: one piece at every slice height, 5.6 times the volume of the one-plane solid, and no waist where the flat bodies touch (cross-section at x = -0.618 is 119 % of the section through the centre; the one-plane rule gives 3.8 %, the folded rule 2.3 %). Its Mandelbrot solid is a smooth fat body with sprays of spikes. No bodies, no beads.

2. The both-planes-exact pillow (pillowboth) is the nearest a pillow has come and is still one lump. Both planes are exact (2.5e-15 and 2.8e-15), nothing jumps, the fin is gone, and the bodies get waists (27 % and 17 % of the centre section), but the waists never close: the slice at z = 0.2 is one piece where the one-plane and folded rules give three separate ovals. The picture is a fibrous, dusty diamond.

3. Is it the nature of a direction map that is chaotic on the whole sphere? Not of chaos as such: the folded rule also stretches every direction and it draws bodies. What the two rules that draw bodies share, and no pillow has, I measured: around every point of the plane, including the direction (-1, 0, 0), they are a plain turn-and-scale (sideways stretch 2.000 = in-plane stretch 2.000, image goes round once). A pillow has to wrap three sheets around three directions of the plane z = 0 (60, 180, 300 degrees), and 180 degrees is the negative x-axis, where the flat sets' touching points sit. A smooth rule can only do that with sideways stretch 0 (measured 0.0000007), so everything near the negative x-axis is crushed onto the axis and stays bounded with it: a solid sleeve, hence the egg. A creased rule keeps some stretch there (radial 0.66 to 1.99, both 1.08 to 2.80) and the waist narrows as that gets nearer an even 2 (119 % -> 74 % -> 27 %), but the stretching copies every crease onto a dense set of surfaces, which is the fibrous look. Smooth pillow = rock, creased pillow = fibres. This part is measured at one direction and argued to first order, not proved.

4. Thickness: the pillow Mandelbrot solids are 3.5 to 5.4 times as tall as the one-plane lens (half height 0.98 to 1.51 against 0.28), about as tall as the folded solid (1.04). Just off the plane the pillowboth basilica slice is LARGER than the flat set (108 % at z = 0.02; one plane 98 %): the flat set sits in a shallow groove.

5. Worth showing the user? Not as a candidate. pillowboth: no (ugly, 2.7 times slower, and its z = 0 picture is drawn 6 to 9 % too fat). pillowsmooth is the only clean pillow picture and is cheap, but its z = 0 slice is not the flat set (51 % of the Mandelbrot set's area differs, the "basilica" slice is an egg 2.25 times too big); at most a history entry labelled "reference, not exact", or one picture explaining why the pillow route is closed. The one pillow idea not built is a layout with an even threefold cone (stretch exactly 2 in every direction) at the three wrap directions; it would still be creased everywhere. The measurements point away from pillows: keep each plane a turn-and-scale.

43 minutes used (23:31 to 00:14).
cands.formulas:
PILLOWSMOOTH (approach id "pillowsmooth"; power 2, and 4 / 8 by repeating):
  F(v) = |v|^2 * L(v/|v|)
  L(d), d = (x, y, z) unit:
    w = (x + i*y) / (1 + |z|)                 (chart of the lower half sphere, |w| <= 1)
    N = 2*w^3 - 1;  D = w*(2 - w^3);  q = |N|^2 + |D|^2
    L(d) = ( 2*Re(N*conj(D))/q, 2*Im(N*conj(D))/q, s*(|N|^2 - |D|^2)/q ),  s = -1 if z > 0, +1 if z < 0
    input z exactly 0 -> output z exactly 0
  This is w -> (2w^3 - 1)/(w(2 - w^3)) with w = (x + iy)/(1 - z). The map commutes with the mirror z -> -z, so the upper half is computed as the mirror image; N and D are kept as a pair so nothing is divided by zero.
  Power dial: n < 1.5 returns v; 1.5 <= n < 3 one application, length |v|^2; 3 <= n < 6 two, |v|^4; n >= 6 three, |v|^8. In the shader sqr uses dot(v, v) directly.

PILLOWBOTH (approach id "pillowboth"; m = round(n)):
  F_m(v) = |v|^m * Phi(m * PhiInv(v/|v|));  m = 0 -> (1,0,0);  |v| < 1e-20 -> 0 for m > 0.
  Sheet arithmetic exactly as out/proto/radial: l = INVERSE(d.x, d.y, |d.z|); X = l if d.z >= 0 else (lA + lC, lB + lC, -lC); Y = (m*XA - (m - 1), m*XB, m*XC); i = floor(Y), f = Y - i, S = fA + fB + fC, colour k = (iB - iC) mod 3; g = (1,0,0) if S < 0.5 or S >= 2.5, (1 - fA, 1 - fC, 1 - fB) if 1.5 < S < 2.5 (flip: lower half sphere), else f; weights[(k + j) mod 3] = g[j]; D = LAYOUT(weights), D.z negated if flip; if the input z is exactly 0 the output z is set to 0.
  LAYOUT(lA, lB, lC) -> direction with z >= 0, T = 2*pi/3:
    mn = min(lA, lB, lC); e = 3*mn; s = 1 - e
    k = 0 if lC is least (edge AB), else 1 if lA <= lB (edge BC), else 2 (edge CA); next = lB, lC, lA for k = 0, 1, 2
    t = clamp((next - mn)/s, 0, 1), or 1/2 when s = 0
    p = (cos(pi*e/2)*cos(T*(k + t)), cos(pi*e/2)*sin(T*(k + t)), sin(pi*e/2))
    SLIDE: c = hypot(p.x, p.z)
      p.x >= 0: a = (4/3)*atan2(p.z, p.x);   (x, z) = c*(cos a, sin a)
      p.x <  0: b = (2/3)*atan2(p.z, -p.x);  (x, z) = c*(-cos b, sin b)       y unchanged
  INVERSE(x, y, z >= 0) -> weights:
    UNSLIDE: c = hypot(x, z); if z + sqrt(3)*x >= 0: a = (3/4)*atan2(z, x), (x, z) = c*(cos a, sin a); else b = (3/2)*atan2(z, -x), (x, z) = c*(-cos b, sin b)
    e = atan2(z, hypot(x, y)) * 2/pi;  a = atan2(y, x)/T, plus 3 if negative;  k = min(floor(a), 2);  t = a - k
    weights = e/3 each, plus (1 - e)*(1 - t) on corner k and (1 - e)*t on corner k + 1
  The slide is the maths check's first alternative (tau' = (4/3) tau up to 90 degrees, (2/3) tau + 60 degrees after), with the second branch written from the far side so that z = 0 stays exactly 0. Face centres land at (-1/2, 0, +-sqrt(3)/2).

Both: mul(a, b) of two different points is the one-plane sphere-inversion product (aprMmul), cmap is the identity.
